result.title: PoseBench: Probing Pose Awareness in Visual Foundation Models
result.summary: Pose awareness characterizes the extent to which a learned feature space aligns with the underlying object-pose manifold, such that observations with similar poses exhibit greater feature similarity than those with increasingly different poses. While such structure is desirable for pose-sensitive 3D vision tasks, visual foundation models pre-trained on individual 2D images typically lack explicit 3D or pose supervision. This raises a fundamental question: Do 2D visual foundation models exhibit pose awareness after large-scale pretraining? To answer this question, we introduce PoseBench, a systematic benchmark to probe pose awareness in pretrained visual features. Our evaluation follows a progressive design: held-out rendered views probe intrinsic pose-aware structure under controlled conditions, while real-image queries evaluate how robustly this structure remains accessible under real-world variations. We further introduce pose-graph-based refinement as a complementary probe of compatibility between feature neighborhoods and the underlying pose manifold. Across 31 publicly available checkpoints from 10 pretraining families, PoseBench reveals that pose awareness is an implicit but non-uniform property of 2D visual foundation models, and consistent gains from pose-graph refinement suggest that feature spaces retain structure compatible with the underlying pose manifold. PoseBench therefore provides a systematic basis for understanding and selecting pretrained features for pose-sensitive 3D vision tasks.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 PoseBench，用受控渲染视角、真实图像查询与姿态图精化探针，系统检验 31 个 2D 预训练视觉基础模型的特征空间是否与物体姿态流形对齐，即是否具备「姿态感知」结构。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「特征相似度是否反映底层几何流形」的探针设计与 LVR 中 latent 是否保留视觉细节、几何与任务必要信息的评价问题相通，可能为刻画 latent 表示几何提供可核查的评价思路；但该工作针对 3D 姿态而非推理期状态生成，联系较间接。
